Definition: from the base of G939 (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively):--firm, of force, stedfast, sure.
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible bebaios means firm, steadfast, sure, and it appears 8 times across the Bible. Peter tells believers to make their calling and election sure, and Paul says the promise is sure to all the seed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what God says is firm, not shaky, and my hope is sure because the One who promised it does not move. That is why I keep coming back to it: bebaios is not a word to rush past.
